  • 探討後黃仁勳時代對美國 AI 資料中心建設、融資擔保以及美中晶片監管政策的潛在連鎖衝擊。
  • 剖析台灣半導體與伺服器供應鏈（如台積電、廣達、緯創等）所面臨的訂單風險與轉型機遇。

摘要

黃仁勳震撼交棒，輝達短期穩健但長線考驗接班智慧

作者指出，輝達董事會突然宣布黃仁勳辭去執行長職務，由財務長柯蕾特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）暫代職務。消息公布初期引發市場震盪，但散戶迅速進場承接，市場普遍認為輝達已非一人公司，單季營收規模龐大且未來一至兩年的晶片設計與生產排程早已確立，短期出貨受衝擊有限。然而，長期隱憂在於黃仁勳過去親力親為建立的亞洲供應鏈同盟與個人魅力，非工程師出身的克雷斯及未來的正式接班人是否能維持強大技術視野與擴張野心，將是輝達能否維持 AI 霸權的最大關鍵。

外溢效應擴大：AI資料中心建置放緩與政策風向轉變

作者分析，這場人事地震的漣漪將波及更廣泛的實體產業。輝達以往在 AI 生態系中扮演如「中央銀行」的角色，曾為大型資料中心建設提供巨額租金與電力擔保，一旦新管理團隊收緊擔保策略，可能引發AI 資料中心建設延宕，進而打擊美國營造與設備製造業。同時在政策層面，黃仁勳過去在白宮與國會具備極大影響力，隨著其卸任以及美國政局變動，美國對中國的晶片禁令限制可能進一步收緊，並對現行依賴輝達晶片的開源 AI 生態系造成劇烈衝擊。

台灣供應鏈的轉機與挑戰，以及傳奇領袖的遠見啟示

針對台灣產業鏈，作者提到台廠雖擔憂輝達未來擴產速度可能趨緩，但即使美國科技巨頭分散訂單至 AMD 等競爭對手，由於先進晶片仍多由台積電代工、伺服器組裝亦仰賴廣達與緯創等台廠，台灣業者依然具備承接多元訂單的彈性與優勢。影片最後，作者回顧了黃仁勳的領導特質，從 2006 年頂住質疑重金押注 CUDA 技術，到早年歷經瀕臨破產所磨練出的強烈危機意識，正是黃仁勳超前的遠見奠定了輝達今日的無可替代性。

================================================

Jensen Huang has actually resigned. Nvidia's board announced on the 12th that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO and board member, effective immediately . Until the board finds a successor, CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO . Nvidia’s stock fell by about 10%in early trading Thursday, so today we will discuss what the post-Jensen Huang era at Nvidia will look like. The Jensen Huang turmoil this time. Hello everyone, I am Fan Qifei, welcome to Fan Qifei's World View. After Jensen Huang announced his resignation, Nvidia's stock price plummeted by 14%at one point, but the decline narrowed to 4.3%by the close. Interestingly, according to market research data, within just 30 minutes of the US market opening that day, retail investors poured $ 111 million into buying Nvidia stock, marking the strongest opening buy-in ever recorded by the firm. Why is that? Because many investors. believe that while Jensen Huang is important, the company's competitive advantage has long since ceased to depend on him alone. The Financial Times interviewed an investment firm executive who pointed out that Nvidia became a four-trillion-dollar company not because Jensen Huang sits in the CEO chair, but because the company’s revenue last quarter reached $ 100 billion, doubling year-over-year. More importantly, Nvidia’s short-term product development and launch plans are basically set. Reuters cited a fund manager holding Nvidia shares who analyzed that the.

chips Nvidia plans to release in the next one to two years are already designed and in production, so the impact on short-term shipments is expected to be limited. In other words, even if the boss changes now, it is unlikely to immediately disrupt the product launch schedule. But surviving in the short term doesn't mean there is no long-term crisis; just as we mentioned yesterday, the real question is: where is the next Jensen Huang? What Jensen Huang has been most famous for in recent years is the "Jensen Huang whirlwind" he stirred up. For years, he. has visited Asia frequently, personally managing partnerships with companies like TSMC, Foxconn, and South Korea’s SK Hynix, making this whirlwind blow not only into Taiwan's night markets but also into Korea. So the question now is : Jensen Huang has spent years building rapport with these major Asian tech firms, and while he has connected a vast Nvidia supply chain and even expanded cooperation to robots and AI factories, can the next CEO continue these partnerships? Currently, 59-year-old CFO Colette Kress is temporarily taking the. helm at Nvidia. Although she is not a chip engineer, she has been a key behind-the-scenes player in helping Jensen Huang build his AI empire over the past 13 years, and her credentials are quite impressive. She previously worked at Texas Instruments for eight years, Microsoft for 13 years, and also served as a senior financial executive at Cisco. In 2013, Jensen Huang personally recruited him to join Nvidia , which was then known only for gaming graphics cards. Surprisingly, he took the advice of his eight and ten-year-old sons and decided to join.

Fortune magazine noted that Nvidia was the smallest company he had worked for at the time. Yet, during his tenure as CFO, annual revenue skyrocketed from $ 4.1 billion to $ 215.9 billion in 2026— a 50-fold increase. He did more than just manage money. He helped the company establish management systems to support rapid expansion, becoming a key strategic partner to Jensen Huang. Forbes once listed her among the world's most powerful businesswomen, and she was even ranked 32nd on the list of. America's richest self-made women, with Nvidia stock holdings worth about $ 750 million. However, being good with money doesn't mean replacing Jensen Huang's technical vision. She is currently only the interim CEO, and the board is still searching for a permanent successor. Whether she can step from behind the scenes to lead Nvidia's continued dominance in the AI market will be a major test. Research firms warn that if product development direction becomes unclear or execution slows down after the leadership change. Competitors could seize the opportunity to catch up. The real question is whether Nvidia will continue to expand as aggressively after Jensen Huang departs. Research analysts are looking at how the post-Jensen era at Nvidia will impact AI data center supply chains and startups on a large scale. So, next, we will talk about what other impacts there might be outside of Nvidia . Because the ripples from Jensen.

Huang’s resignation won't just affect Nvidia; the consequences could reach the U.S. construction industry, especially in Taiwan. Let’s break it down one by one. First, the construction industry: besides selling chips, Nvidia has been described by The New York Times as the central bank of the AI industry. For example, this August, OpenAI leased a massive data center in Ohio. For this project alone, Nvidia provided guarantees for over a hundred billion dollars in rent and electricity costs. Simply put, with Nvidia’s backing, developers can more easily borrow money to build facilities, and Nvidia, in turn. , gets the chance to sell more chips. Now that Jensen Huang is gone, if new management is more cautious about guaranteeing new projects and other investors don't step in, some data centers could see construction delays. In recent years, the U.S. construction and equipment manufacturing sectors have relied on these projects for business. If construction slows, orders will also be pushed back. But the stock market might react faster. If investors start questioning how long it will take for these massive data center investments to pay off, and proceed to dump AI stocks,. households seeing their portfolios shrink may cut spending, spreading the impact to other industries. However, on the day Jensen Huang resigned, the stock price drop had a relatively limited impact on the broader US market. What we need to watch next is how many of those planned data centers will still be able to secure funding to proceed as scheduled. Next is policy. In the past, Jensen Huang held significant influence over the White House; he wasn't just close with Trump, but could even sway certain US chip policies. Analysts point out that while Trump originally aligned with Silicon Valley’s tech faction to.

ease restrictions and cash in on AI, Huang’s national security concerns— coupled with a shift in Congress—mean this honeymoon period is effectively over. Moving forward, the Democrat-controlled Congress may pressure the Department of Commerce to strictly enforce existing chip bans, or even further restrict which chips can be sold to China. Research firms warn this will also impact open-source AI development. Huang previously pushed hard to open-source base code so developers could run AI at a lower cost, but now. that leading open-source models are being developed in China using NVIDIA chips—and with US developers using them —analysts believe Huang’s departure will disrupt this entire ecosystem. Finally, let’s focus on the impact on Taiwan. After Huang’s resignation, Taiwanese suppliers were first concerned about whether their existing orders would be affected. While we've noted that NVIDIA chip production for the next two to three years remains largely stable, some supply chain executives told Reuters their greater concern is the pace of expansion. They said if the. new CEO doesn't lock in production capacity as early as Huang did, they might slow down their own expansion. After all, building factories and buying equipment requires upfront capital; suppliers have to think twice before investing if clients haven't confirmed their order volumes. And if major US clients start splitting their next batch of orders with other chip companies, can Taiwanese firms still win those contracts? Take Facebook's parent company, Meta, for example. Reports suggest that even before Huang's departure, Meta was already signing contracts with NVIDIA while simultaneously placing large orders with.

AMD. Is this bad news for Taiwan? Not necessarily. First, both NVIDIA and AMD are only responsible for chip design; the actual manufacturing is done by TSMC . Second, regarding servers, Taiwanese firms are also involved there. For instance, Wistron already handles assembly, and AMD has also tapped Wistron, Inventec, and Quanta to build AI servers. So even if major clients buy more AMD chips, Taiwanese manufacturers still have opportunities to win business . However, switching chips requires adjustments to server power supply and. cooling, so how much they get depends on their progress in collaborating on these new platforms. If US tech giants decide to delay building their data centers, then regardless of which chips they ultimately choose, Taiwanese manufacturers may have to wait longer before they can secure their next orders . Having discussed Nvidia in the post-Jensen Huang era, I’d finally like to talk about the person, Jensen Huang himself. The New Yorker published a 5,000-word profile on Jensen Huang that I highly recommend reading. I will only. highlight a few key points: First, his preemptive deployment in AI, betting correctly on the technological revolution of the next decade. As early as 2006, Huang began investing in the CUDA platform, enabling graphics cards originally meant for gaming to be used for scientific computing. But there were few clients then, and Wall Street was skeptical. By the end of 2008, Nvidia's stock plummeted by 70%, until a major breakthrough in AI research in 2012 proved his bet was right, establishing Nvidia’s future dominance in AI. Second.

, having once nearly gone bankrupt, he developed a strong sense of crisis. In 1996, because Nvidia bet on the wrong technical direction, they were forced to lay off over half their staff and poured their remaining funds into an untested new chip. At the time, the company only had enough money left to pay one month of salaries. Fortunately, they rebounded , which instilled in Huang a keen sense of crisis, leaving behind his famous corporate motto: "Our company is always 30 days away from going out of business ." Third, being bullied in childhood forged his ability to survive in. adversity. When Huang was 9, he was sent to a religious boarding school in Kentucky; by 17, he bore scars from knife wounds. He faced long-term racial discrimination, with classmates even trying to shake him off a suspension bridge. Yet he wasn't defeated; instead , he believes this experience taught him how to survive in adversity. Fourth, his management style is strict, leaving employees both in awe and afraid. Huang sends hundreds of emails daily and requires employees to report their five most important tasks each week. He often questions junior engineers directly and. is prone to losing his temper over unsatisfactory answers. One employee described interacting with him like sticking a finger into an electrical outlet; a research executive admitted they are sometimes afraid of him, yet they also believe he cares for them. Every time Jensen Huang visits Taiwan, it causes a sensation with wall-to-wall media coverage. Does this description from The New Yorker match the Jensen Huang you know? Everyone today is talking about what Nvidia would be like without Jensen Huang, but I'm curious to know what Jensen Huang would be like if he were no longer Nvidia's CEO. Today I.

want to ask you all, do you own NVIDIA stock? Do you have confidence in NVIDIA without Jensen Huang? Leave a comment to let me know, and if you like this show, be sure to share it with more people. You can also subscribe to the LDay official account; it pushes important news, including this show, to your phone every day. 摘要

爭議引發的接班疑問

影片中，作者范先回顧黃仁勳先前遭遇的中國間諜疑雲，接著提到外媒新近報導指稱，黃仁勳涉嫌與一名輝達高階主管有婚外情。這些消息尚待調查與查證，卻已加深外界對公司治理的疑慮，也讓輝達董事會可能如何處理黃仁勳去留成為焦點。作者認為，比起個人爭議，更值得關注的是：如果黃仁勳突然無法任職，輝達是否有明確的接班安排？

高度集中的管理與治理問題

影片引述《紐約時報》的調查指出，黃仁勳不喜歡傳統的多層管理架構，曾有超過六十名高階主管直接向他報告，重大決策也常由他親自掌握。這種管理方式伴隨輝達從遊戲顯示卡公司成長為人工智慧晶片龍頭，但也讓外界擔心，公司的決策與方向是否過度集中在一人身上。

影片也提到，黃仁勳的兒子、女兒與女婿都在輝達任職。輝達表示，相關家人並非法定高階主管，且不直接向黃仁勳報告；然而，部分員工仍對家人與高層之間的接觸及其可能形成的權力關係感到疑慮。董事會方面，影片指出其成員多數任職多年，公司也沒有董事長職位，而是由首席獨立董事協調運作。部分治理學者因此質疑，董事會能否在調查中保持足夠獨立，並對執行長進行有效監督。

作者將接班疑問分成幾個面向。首先，外界看不到明確的「第二號人物」，不像蘋果曾由史蒂夫・賈伯斯安排提姆・庫克接班。影片引用商學院學者的看法，認為董事會應培養至少兩名潛在接班人，或預先掌握外部接任人選，確保執行長若突然離任，公司仍能持續運作。

其次，黃仁勳的價值不只在管理，也包括對技術趨勢的判斷。他及早押注 GPU 用於人工智慧，輝達又建立了涵蓋晶片、軟體平台、網路技術與雲端客戶合作的競爭優勢。影片稱，輝達在大型人工智慧專案晶片市場占有率約九成，因此若黃仁勳離開，股價可能承受壓力；但公司的技術與競爭力也不會因單一人物離開而立即消失。

此外，影片談到美國國會可能推動更嚴格的人工智慧監管，例如要求大型模型接受獨立安全測試、釐清企業造成損害時的法律責任，以及加強資料中心監督。作者指出，政策不會一夕改變，但國會調查、法律風險與監管不確定性，可能提高科技公司的股價與融資壓力；若模型審查趨嚴、資料中心建設放緩，全球人工智慧投資成長也可能受到影響。

台灣供應鏈與經濟的牽連

最後，作者把焦點轉向台灣，指出台灣供應鏈與輝達關係緊密。影片引用台積電二〇二五年財報資料稱，最大客戶貢獻近百分之十九營收，約新台幣七千二百七十億元，並指該客戶為輝達；鴻海、廣達與緯創等廠商也參與人工智慧伺服器供應鏈。影片並稱，輝達在台灣有超過五百家合作夥伴，黃仁勳曾表示公司每年在台支出達一千億美元，並可能增至一千五百億美元。大綱在此處中止，尚未完整交代作者對台灣經濟衝擊的後續分析；但前述內容已凸顯，輝達若出現重大變局，影響可能延伸至台灣的重要科技供應鏈。

摘要

爭議引發的接班疑問

影片中，作者范先回顧黃仁勳先前遭遇的中國間諜疑雲，接著提到外媒新近報導指稱，黃仁勳涉嫌與一名輝達高階主管有婚外情。這些消息尚待調查與查證，卻已加深外界對公司治理的疑慮，也讓輝達董事會可能如何處理黃仁勳去留成為焦點。作者認為，比起個人爭議，更值得關注的是：如果黃仁勳突然無法任職，輝達是否有明確的接班安排？

高度集中的管理與治理問題

影片引述《紐約時報》的調查指出，黃仁勳不喜歡傳統的多層管理架構，曾有超過六十名高階主管直接向他報告，重大決策也常由他親自掌握。這種管理方式伴隨輝達從遊戲顯示卡公司成長為人工智慧晶片龍頭，但也讓外界擔心，公司的決策與方向是否過度集中在一人身上。

影片也提到，黃仁勳的兒子、女兒與女婿都在輝達任職。輝達表示，相關家人並非法定高階主管，且不直接向黃仁勳報告；然而，部分員工仍對家人與高層之間的接觸及其可能形成的權力關係感到疑慮。董事會方面，影片指出其成員多數任職多年，公司也沒有董事長職位，而是由首席獨立董事協調運作。部分治理學者因此質疑，董事會能否在調查中保持足夠獨立，並對執行長進行有效監督。

輝達是否有黃仁勳以外的支柱

作者將接班疑問分成幾個面向。首先，外界看不到明確的「第二號人物」，不像蘋果曾由史蒂夫・賈伯斯安排提姆・庫克接班。影片引用商學院學者的看法，認為董事會應培養至少兩名潛在接班人，或預先掌握外部接任人選，確保執行長若突然離任，公司仍能持續運作。

其次，黃仁勳的價值不只在管理，也包括對技術趨勢的判斷。他及早押注 GPU 用於人工智慧，輝達又建立了涵蓋晶片、軟體平台、網路技術與雲端客戶合作的競爭優勢。影片稱，輝達在大型人工智慧專案晶片市場占有率約九成，因此若黃仁勳離開，股價可能承受壓力；但公司的技術與競爭力也不會因單一人物離開而立即消失。

股價、調查情境與監管風向

影片引述路透社報導，輝達股價在兩個交易日內下跌約百分之九點五，市值蒸發約新台幣十四兆元；作者也提醒，市場原本就擔憂人工智慧投資過熱，以及科技公司大舉投入後能否獲得回報，相關股東訴訟亦在追問公司是否充分揭露風險。印度財經媒體提出數種可能發展，包括調查未發現不當行為、董事會加強監督、黃仁勳因隱瞞重要資訊而離任，或調查揭露更嚴重的資安與治理問題；即使未被認定違法，他也可能自行離職，促使公司啟動接班程序。

此外，影片談到美國國會可能推動更嚴格的人工智慧監管，例如要求大型模型接受獨立安全測試、釐清企業造成損害時的法律責任，以及加強資料中心監督。作者指出，政策不會一夕改變，但國會調查、法律風險與監管不確定性，可能提高科技公司的股價與融資壓力；若模型審查趨嚴、資料中心建設放緩，全球人工智慧投資成長也可能受到影響。

台灣供應鏈與經濟的牽連

最後，作者把焦點轉向台灣，指出台灣供應鏈與輝達關係緊密。影片引用台積電二〇二五年財報資料稱，最大客戶貢獻近百分之十九營收，約新台幣七千二百七十億元，並指該客戶為輝達；鴻海、廣達與緯創等廠商也參與人工智慧伺服器供應鏈。影片並稱，輝達在台灣有超過五百家合作夥伴，黃仁勳曾表示公司每年在台支出達一千億美元，並可能增至一千五百億美元。大綱在此處中止，尚未完整交代作者對台灣經濟衝擊的後續分析；但前述內容已凸顯，輝達若出現重大變局，影響可能延伸至台灣的重要科技供應鏈。
